title: Types of Reactions
description: The main ways chemical reactions are classified, with the general form, how to recognize each, and worked examples.

modes.label: Equation → Reaction type
modes.question: What type of reaction is this? {equation}

modes.label: General form → Reaction type
modes.question: Which type of reaction follows the pattern {form}?

types.name: Synthesis
types.summary: Two or more simple substances combine to form one more complex product.
recognize: Several reactants, one product.
Often two elements forming a compound, or a compound adding to another to make a bigger one.
Usually releases energy.
realWorld: The Haber process joins nitrogen and hydrogen to make ammonia for fertilizer.
Quicklime (CaO) reacts with water to form slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂, used in mortar.
Iron rusting: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.

types.name: Decomposition
types.summary: One compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
recognize: One reactant, several products.
Needs an input of energy: heat, light or electricity.
It is the opposite of synthesis.
realWorld: Electrolysis splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.
Heating limestone (CaCO₃) gives lime and carbon dioxide, a step in making cement.
Sodium azide in a car airbag decomposes to nitrogen gas in milliseconds.

types.name: Single replacement
types.summary: One element takes the place of another element in a compound.
recognize: An element and a compound on the left, a different element and a different compound on the right.
A metal replaces another metal (or hydrogen) only if it is more reactive. A halogen replaces a less reactive halogen.
The activity series predicts whether the reaction will happen.
realWorld: An iron nail dropped in copper sulfate solution becomes coated with copper.
Zinc dissolving in acid gives off hydrogen gas.
A zinc coating protects steel because zinc is more reactive than iron.

types.name: Double replacement
types.summary: Two compounds swap partners to form two new compounds.
recognize: Two compounds on each side, usually ionic compounds dissolved in water.
It goes forward when a product leaves the solution: an insoluble solid (a precipitate), a gas, or water.
No electrons are transferred, so it is not a redox reaction.
realWorld: Adding silver nitrate to a solution that contains chloride makes a white precipitate of AgCl, a classic test.
Hard water forms scale (CaCO₃) when calcium and carbonate ions meet.
Water treatment can remove dissolved metals by precipitating them.

types.name: Combustion
types.summary: A substance reacts quickly with oxygen and releases heat and light. For a hydrocarbon fuel the products are carbon dioxide and water.
recognize: Oxygen is a reactant.
A hydrocarbon or alcohol on the left, CO₂ and H₂O on the right.
Strongly exothermic.
With too little oxygen, combustion is incomplete and gives carbon monoxide or soot instead.
realWorld: Gas stoves, furnaces and car engines.
A burning candle.
Cellular respiration is a slow, controlled form of the same reaction with glucose.

types.name: Acid–base
types.summary: An acid reacts with a base to form a salt and water.
recognize: An acid (a source of H⁺) and a base (a source of OH⁻) are the reactants.
The products are an ionic salt and water.
It is a special case of double replacement.
The net ionic equation is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O.
realWorld: Antacids neutralize excess stomach acid.
Farmers add lime to acidic soil.
Baking soda is used to neutralize an acid spill.

types.name: Redox
types.summary: A reaction in which electrons move from one species to another. The species that loses electrons is oxidized, and the one that gains them is reduced.
recognize: Oxidation numbers change.
OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain, of electrons.
It overlaps the other types. Many synthesis, decomposition, single replacement and combustion reactions are redox. Double replacement and acid–base reactions are not.
The oxidizing agent is the species that gets reduced, and the reducing agent is the species that gets oxidized.
realWorld: Batteries turn a redox reaction into electric current.
Rusting of iron.
Bleach works by oxidizing stains.

items.note: A halogen replaces a less reactive halogen.
